Kuvitus: hämärässä luokassa pöydällä on: Illustration: in a dim classroom, a laser pointer and a torch on a desk point at the same white screen. A thin red beam leaves the laser pointer and hits the screen as a small bright dot. The light of the torch spreads into a wide cone and lights a large, dim, yellowish area of the screen.
Kolme tapahtumaa vierekkäin, kaavakuva,: Three events side by side, schematic figure, not to scale. Each has two energy levels of an atom, the lower E1 and the upper E2, and the blue dot is an electron; the ring shows where it was before the event. On the left absorption: a photon whose energy hf is the difference of the levels enters the atom and lifts the electron to the level E2, and the photon disappears. In the middle spontaneous emission: the electron drops by itself from the level E2 to the level E1, and a photon leaves in a random direction, here obliquely upwards. On the right stimulated emission: an incoming photon makes the electron of an excited atom drop, and two identical photons leave the atom in the same direction and in step.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: tehon 1,0 milliwa: Graph to scale: the number of photons per second emitted by a laser of power 1.0 milliwatt as a function of the wavelength. On the horizontal axis the wavelength from zero to 700 nanometres, on the vertical axis the number of photons per second in units of 10 to the power 15 photons per second, from zero to 3.5. The graph is a straight line through the origin. Three laser pointers are marked on it: violet 405 nm, 2.04; green 532 nm, 2.68; and red 650 nm, 3.27. With the same power, a laser of a longer wavelength emits more photons, because one photon carries less energy.
Kolmitasoisen laseraineen, kuten rubiini: The energy levels of a three-level laser medium, such as ruby, schematic figure, not to scale. At the bottom is the ground state E1, at the top the short-lived level E3 and between them the long-lived level E2. Green arrow: pumping lifts atoms from the level E1 to the level E3. Grey dashed arrow: the atoms move from the level E3 quickly and without light to the level E2. Red arrow: the laser transition from the level E2 to the level E1, wavelength 694 nm. The blue dots are atoms: on the level E2 there are seven and on the level E1 four, so the upper level has more atoms than the lower. This is called population inversion.
Laserin rakenne, kaavakuva, ei mittakaav: The structure of a laser, schematic figure, not to scale. In the middle is a horizontal rod of active medium. At its left end is a mirror that reflects all the light, and at its right end a mirror that reflects 99 percent and lets 1 percent through. Under the rod is a pump lamp whose light lifts atoms to the excited state. Inside the rod red photons travel along the axis back and forth between the mirrors and multiply. Two photons leave obliquely sideways and exit the rod. A narrow red laser beam comes out through the right mirror.
Viisi kvanttipistettä allekkain, halkais: Five quantum dots one under another, their diameters to scale with each other, each drawn in the colour of the light it emits. Diameter 2.0 nm: wavelength 480 nm, photon energy 2.58 eV, cyan. 3.0 nm: 530 nm, 2.34 eV, green. 4.0 nm: 570 nm, 2.18 eV, yellow-green. 5.0 nm: 600 nm, 2.07 eV, orange. 6.0 nm: 620 nm, 2.00 eV, red. The smaller the dot, the shorter the wavelength and the greater the photon energy.
Periaatekuva tunneloitumisesta, ei mitta: Schematic figure of tunnelling, not to scale. An electron arrives from the left; its energy E, the horizontal dashed line, is smaller than the height of the grey barrier in the middle. The blue area shows the probability of detecting the electron: on the left of the barrier it is large, inside the barrier it decreases quickly, and on the right of the barrier it is small but not zero. So the electron can be found behind the barrier even though its energy is not enough to get over the barrier.
